newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money rises on liquidity shortage.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money rises on liquidity shortage.

text.p: Dutch call money rates were under considerable upward pressure on Tuesday as settlements for the government's DTC programmes created an enduring shortage of liquidity.

Money market dealers said the current allocation under the special advances pact was too tight as a substantial amount of cash was flowing out of the market as a result of the Dutch Treasury Certificate (DTC) programmes.
"The market was at least one billion guilders short of liquidity today," said one dealer, adding the pressure on call money would continue for at least two more days.
Call money was bid as high as 3.00 percent earlier, but the rate edged somewhat lower in mid-afternoon to around 2.75 percent. This was still well above the special advances rate of 2.50 percent.
The Agency of the Dutch Ministry of Finance said earlier today it had raised another 1.4 billion guilders through its DTC programmes during the last week.
The Agency said the payment date for new DTC contracts was usually set after the announcement of a new special advances pact.

"Usually, payment is during the next pact," the Agency said. A later payment date was also possible, but in times of government cash shortage settlements could also happen during the current advances pact.
Dealers said they expected the new cash reserve again to be set at nil or liquidity would be squeezed even further.

The central bank will announce a new cash reserve at 1500 GMT. It sets a cash reserve to cream off excess money market liquidity, forcing commercial banks to draw down their liquid funds to meet the cash reserve requirement.
